nodes_add.name: Mahadevendra Saraswati V
nodes_add.note: Born Lakshmikantan; 67th head of the Kanchi Kamakoti monastery for about a week (6-13 February 1907); maternal cousin of Chandrasekharendra Saraswati (Mahadevan). Samadhi at Kalavai.

nodes_add.name: Jayendra Saraswati
nodes_add.note: Born Subrahmanyam, 18 July 1935; given the name Jayendra Saraswati 22 March 1954; 69th head of the Kanchi monastery; arrested 11 November 2004 and charged with murder and criminal conspiracy in the Sankararaman case; acquitted with all co-accused by the Principal District and Sessions Court, Puducherry, 27 November 2013; no appeal filed; died 28 February 2018.

nodes_update.name: Chandrasekharendra Saraswati
nodes_update.note: Swaminathan; the Kanchi Paramacharya, 68th head of the Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham from 13 February 1907 to his death on 8 January 1994. Orthodox counterpoint in Part 2: one God behind all religions, but no conversion and varna by birth. Talks compiled as Deivathin Kural (English: Hindu Dharma).

edges_upsert.note: Kanchi Kamakoti matha's line from Adi Shankara. The institution's antiquity before the 18th century is disputed (Sringeri; V. R. Sharma 1987; K. P. Sunil 1987; Vidyasankar Sundaresan 2000); the matha's chronology dates its founding to 482 BCE, and T. A. Gopinatha Rao (1916) read copper plates as placing it at Kanchipuram until 1686.
Emergency succession at Kalavai on 13 February 1907 after the deaths of the 66th and 67th heads within about a week.
Sannyasa and the name Jayendra Saraswati given at Kanchipuram, 22 March 1954 (Mahadevan).
Met at Chingleput in January 1931; declined to take Brunton as disciple and sent him to Ramana Maharshi (Brunton, A Search in Secret India, 1934; Mahadevan).

places.name: Kalavai
places.what: Made 68th head of the monastery, 13 February 1907 (formal installation followed at Kumbakonam, 9 May 1907); samadhis of his two predecessors; golden jubilee 1957.

places.name: Kumbakonam
places.what: The monastery's base during his youth; studied there from about 1909.

places.name: Chengalpattu (Chingleput)
places.what: Met Paul Brunton, January 1931, and sent him to Ramana Maharshi.

places.name: Varanasi
places.what: Reached on 6 October 1934 during the 1919-1939 all-India tour; visited Banaras Hindu University February 1935.

places.name: Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham, Kanchipuram
places.what: First entered as head 25 January 1931; died and buried here, 8-9 January 1994.

places.name: United Nations Headquarters, New York
places.what: His hymn Maithreem Bhajata sung by M. S. Subbulakshmi, 23 October 1966.

glossary.def: Title of the heads of monasteries that trace their line to Adi Shankara; a celibate monk chosen and initiated by his predecessor.
The classical scheme of four social classes (varna) and four stages of life (ashrama), each with its own duties.
Brahmin households following the smriti law books and Vedic rites, worshipping five deities, and usually aligned with Shankara's Advaita.
A 'victory journey': the traditional touring circuit of a Shankaracharya through the country.

issues: chandrasekharendra-saraswati.mdx: RESOLVED (factcheck): 13 February 1907 was the accession at Kalavai; 9 May 1907 was the formal installation at Kumbakonam (Mahadevan, kamakoti.org SageOfKanchi3). Text now says so.

chandrasekharendra-saraswati.mdx: 66th head's death: Mahadevan says he 'attained siddhi at Kalavai' in 1907 without a date; Wikipedia's Mahadevendra Saraswati V page puts the 67th's tenure 6-13 February 1907, implying the 66th died about 6 February 1907. 'Early 1907' kept. Sources also disagree on the 66th's name/number (Chandrasekharendra VI vs VII); chapter does not name him.

chandrasekharendra-saraswati.mdx: Gandhi meeting: Mahadevan says 'the latter half of 1927'; text now says 'later that year'. Gandhi's Kerala tour was October 1927; exact date not confirmed from Collected Works.
chandrasekharendra-saraswati.mdx: RESOLVED (factcheck): author is Varanasi Rajgopal Sharma (V. R. Sharma), per Wikipedia's reference list; 'T. V. Sharma' in its body is an error.
chandrasekharendra-saraswati.mdx: first publication years of Deivathin Kural (Tamil) and of the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan Hindu Dharma not verified; chapter avoids first-edition dates.
chandrasekharendra-saraswati.mdx: no verifiable archival audio or film of him found; marked [to locate]. Photo not added.

chandrasekharendra-saraswati.mdx: Kalavai coordinates conflict: Wikipedia gives 12.68, 79.42; batch has 12.77, 79.42, which fits Mahadevan's 'about ten miles from Arcot' better. Kept verified: false; needs a map check.

chandrasekharendra-saraswati.mdx: Brunton's physical description ('short man in an ochre robe') and the explicit 'promise' come from A Search in Secret India ch. VIII, which the checker could not read in full; Mahadevan confirms 'noble face', the eyes quote and the instruction not to leave South India before meeting Ramana.

Author decision: the chapter does not mention the separate 2002 assault case against Jayendra (auditor Radhakrishnan), in which he was acquitted in 2016; checker left it out as outside the scope of this figure's entry.

chandrasekharendra-saraswati: Born Swaminathan, 20 May 1894, Villupuram; father Subrahmanya Sastri, teacher; mother Mahalakshmi from Eachangudi; Kannada-speaking Smarta family; upanayanam Tindivanam 1905; studied at Kumbakonam c.1909, Mahendramangalam 1911-14; Court of Wards to May 1915 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandrashekharendra_Saraswati_VIII
Quote 'I was stunned by this unexpected turn of events' (Mahadevan 1983, cited) -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandrashekharendra_Saraswati_VIII
67th head Mahadevendra Saraswati V, born 1889 as Lakshmikantan, first cousin, head 6-13 Feb 1907, samadhi at Kalavai -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahadevendra_Saraswati_V

Became 68th pontiff 13 February 1907 at age 13 (sic); died 8 January 1994 at 2:58 pm in Kanchipuram aged 99; one meal a day; did not touch money; quotes 'I have come to know, as none other perhaps, the endless afflictions of humanity', 'When there is no Vedas, where is the need for this mutt?...'; Narasimha Rao attended, burial delayed an hour; burial in salt/sandal pit, danda broken in three; first pontiff buried on Kanchipuram premises; samadhi opened 11 January; speaks English, French -> https://hinduismtoday.com/magazine/march-1994/1994-03-kanchi-saint-attains-maha-samadhi-at-990a/

All-India tour March 1919 to 1939; Palghat 1927 and Gandhi meeting at Nallicheri cattle shed, Sanskrit/Hindi; entered Kanchi 25 January 1931; Brunton at Chingleput January 1931, 'noble face', eyes 'extraordinarily tranquil and beautiful', sent to Ramana; Kasi 6 October 1934; BHU 9 February 1935 at Malaviya's request; Kalighat chaturmasya 1935; Rameswaram abhisheka 10 June 1939; silence over six months -> https://kamakoti.org/kamakoti/articles/SageOfKanchi6.html

Arrived Kanchi 22 June 1953, three years; Jayendra initiated 22 March 1954; 61st birthday 18 May 1954, asked for land endowments; golden jubilee Kalavai 17 March 1957; quote 'Let action be performed well; thus let God be worshipped!' -> https://kamakoti.org/kamakoti/articles/SageOfKanchi8.html

Madras 1957-59; Milton Singer 1955; Koestler 1959; Queen Frederika Dec 1966; Agama-Silpa-Sadas 1962; Sankara memorials Rameswaram 1963, Rishikesh 1967; quotes 'Advaita is not a school among schools of thought', 'Though other systems may quarrel with Advaita, Advaita does not quarrel with them'; evening silence linked to Dakshinamurti; Madhva saint and Muslim Mastan Saheb -> https://kamakoti.org/kamakoti/articles/SageOfKanchi9.html
Brunton referred to Kumbakonam Sankaracharya camping at Chingleput; referred him to Ramana -> https://www.archive.arunachala.org/1347877473
A Search in Secret India published 1934 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Brunton

Quotes on unity of religions: 'All religions have one common ideal...', 'This one God accepts your devotion...', 'So there is no need to abandon the religion of your birth...', no rite of conversion, 'The goal must be unity, not uniformity.' -> https://kamakoti.org/hindudharma/part1/chap6.htm
Quote 'Like the rivers merging in the ocean all these paths have one meeting point, the Paramatman.' -> https://kamakoti.org/hindudharma/part14/chap11.htm

Quotes 'Sri Krsna establishes that an individual owes his caste to his birth', 'naturally develop a liking and aptitude for the family vocation', 'it has become topsy-turvy' -> https://kamakoti.org/hindudharma/part20/chap3.htm
Brahmin duties, 'however small the sum may be' -> https://www.kamakoti.org/hindudharma/part20/chap10.htm

Gave up palanquin, free meals to untouchables, refused to condemn caste despite Gandhi and Nehru, against dowry, quote 'If I myself were to relax them...', Pope 1964 'We should do nothing disrespectful to the pope', opposed Mahasabha black flags, DK portrait with sandals mid-1960s -> https://www.hinduismtoday.com/magazine/may-1993/1993-05-renowned-hindu-saint-begins-hundredth-year/

Deivathin Kural: Ra. Ganapathy edited from tapes; 7 volumes ~1000 pages each; first two volumes translated as Hindu Dharma by Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan -> https://advaita-vedanta.org/archives/advaita-l/2005-May/014586.html

Maithreem Bhajata composed by him, music Vasant Desai, sung by M. S. Subbulakshmi at UN on 23 October 1966 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maithreem_Bhajata ; https://sriramv.com/2018/05/25/ms-subbulakshmi-at-the-united-nations/

Antiquity dispute: 482 BCE founding claim, 509-477 BCE Shankara, Gopinatha Rao 1916 plates (until 1686), Sringeri rejects, Kumbakonam branch of Sringeri 1821, 1842 trustee, Sunil 1987 rewritten history, Fuller and Smith 'spiritual descendants', Veeramani 1988, male Brahmin students -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanchi_Kamakoti_Peetham
Vidyasankar Sundaresan: official list reliable only after 1700s; 1842 priests' protest -> https://list.indology.info/pipermail/indology/2000-September/022632.html
Introduction to Hindu Dharma (World Wisdom 2008); 'Walking God' -> https://worldwisdom.com/author/hh-the-68th-jagadguru-of-kanchi/
1980 camp at Satara; 1978 tour Andhra and Maharashtra; 1983 sannyasa to Vijayendra -> https://hindupedia.com/en/Chandrasekharendra_Saraswati
Jayendra named 22 March 1954, died 28 February 2018 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayendra_Saraswathi

Sankararaman killed 3 September 2004; Jayendra arrested 11 November 2004; case moved to Puducherry; acquitted November 2013 by Puducherry sessions court with Vijayendra and others -> https://english.udayavani.com/article/shankaracharya-overcame-ordeal-of-murder-charge-in-2013/275029

Jayendra left the mutt in 1987 and was readmitted by the senior pontiff; schools and hospitals for the poor -> https://www.thenewsminute.com/opinion/jayendra-saraswathi-controversial-seer-who-took-kanchi-mutt-masses-77205

chandrasekharendra-saraswati.mdx: Kanchi-origin debate: author named as Varanasi Rajgopal Sharma; added Sharma's dispute of Gopinatha Rao's plate readings; 1821 stated as critics' founding date of the Kumbakonam branch (not 'often dated'); Sunil's article dated 1987; Sundaresan's conclusion restated precisely (list reliable from about early 18th century; no firm evidence of a Kanchipuram matha in 1700) and 'the scholar' replaced with 'a writer on Advaita'; David Smith added with Fuller (Wikipedia, citing Scheifinger 2016; Indology list 6 Sept 2000).

chandrasekharendra-saraswati.mdx: Jayendra case rewritten in precise legal terms: arrested 11 Nov 2004 at Mahabubnagar; charged with murder (IPC 302) and conspiracy (120-B) with 22 others; Supreme Court bail 10 Jan 2005; Supreme Court transfer to Puducherry 26 Oct 2005; all acquitted 27 Nov 2013 by the Principal District and Sessions Court, Puducherry, prosecution failing to prove its case and many witnesses hostile; his response ('Dharma has prevailed. Truth has won.', Organiser 30 Nov 2013); no appeal filed, Madras High Court queried this in 2017 (Udayavani 2018; Deccan Chronicle 27 Nov 2013; Open Dec 2013; DT Next 4 May 2017; Wikipedia Sankararaman murder case).
